outputs.L3:
The ablation applicator includes a tubular body defining an inner lumen configured to receive an ablation medium for treating blood vessel tissue. A control mechanism selectively transitions the tubular body between a passive configuration, suitable for insertion and positioning within a blood vessel, and an active configuration for performing tissue ablation.

An ablation-medium supply line is disposed within the inner lumen of the tubular body. The supply line includes multiple openings through which the ablation medium is released into the surrounding lumen. At least some of these openings are arranged along the supply line at predetermined intervals to promote effective thermal contact between the ablation medium and the tubular body, thereby facilitating controlled transfer of thermal energy to the target tissue.

The applicator may additionally include a temperature sensor positioned within the inner lumen to monitor treatment conditions. A return line may also be provided to carry the ablation medium away from the treatment region. The return line can be formed from a material selected to define or support the applicator’s active shape during the ablation procedure.
outputs.L4:
An ablation applicator is designed to treat tissue associated with a blood vessel by delivering a thermal ablation medium in a controlled and spatially distributed manner. The applicator includes an elongated tubular body sized and configured for insertion into or placement along the vessel. During insertion and positioning, the tubular body remains in a passive mode, in which it has a relatively low profile and sufficient flexibility to advance through the anatomy while minimizing trauma to surrounding tissue. Once the applicator reaches the intended treatment region, it can be transitioned to an active ablation mode in which a treatment portion assumes a predetermined operative configuration and establishes thermal contact with the vessel tissue.

A supply line extends through the tubular body and carries the thermal ablation medium from an external source to the active treatment portion. The supply line includes a plurality of perforations arranged at predetermined intervals. These perforations release the medium at selected locations along the applicator, promoting substantially uniform heating or cooling over the desired treatment length. The spacing, size, and number of perforations may be selected according to the vessel dimensions, the required ablation profile, and the thermal characteristics of the medium. Suitable media may include heated or cooled fluids, vapors, gases, or other substances capable of producing tissue ablation through controlled thermal transfer.

The applicator may further include one or more temperature sensors positioned near or within the active treatment portion. A sensor can provide real-time information concerning the temperature of the applicator, the delivered medium, or adjacent tissue. This information may be supplied to a control system that adjusts treatment parameters such as medium temperature, flow rate, pressure, and treatment duration. Temperature feedback helps maintain the selected therapeutic range, improves consistency of the resulting lesion, and reduces the risk of excessive heating or cooling outside the target region.

In some embodiments, a return line is incorporated into the tubular body. In addition to conveying the thermal medium away from the treatment region, the return line may possess sufficient stiffness, elasticity, or shape memory to define the applicator’s active shape. The return line may be preformed or actuated so that, after deployment, it bends, curves, coils, or otherwise moves the active portion into thermal contact with the vessel wall. When the treatment is complete, the applicator may return to its passive, lower-profile configuration to facilitate atraumatic withdrawal.

In use, the applicator is introduced and advanced to the target location while in the passive mode. The active portion is then deployed into its operative shape, and the thermal ablation medium is delivered through the perforated supply line. Heat is transferred between the medium, the tubular body, and the vessel tissue to create a controlled ablation zone. The medium may subsequently be collected through the return line, allowing circulation and limiting unintended exposure of surrounding anatomy. After the desired treatment endpoint has been reached, delivery is stopped, the applicator is returned to the passive mode, and the device is removed.

By combining a selectively deployable tubular body, distributed delivery of a thermal medium, optional temperature monitoring, and a shape-defining return line, the applicator provides controlled and effective ablation along a selected vessel segment. The arrangement supports accurate positioning, consistent thermal contact, predictable lesion formation, and improved protection of adjacent tissue.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can refer to any book, while “the book” points to one particular book understood by the speaker and listener.

Despite its simplicity, “the” plays an essential role in communication. It creates clarity, emphasizes importance, and connects sentences to shared knowledge. Without it, everyday language would often sound vague or unnatural.

The word also appears in famous names and titles, such as *The Beatles*, *The Great Gatsby*, and *The United Kingdom*. In each case, it gives the subject a sense of distinction or uniqueness. Thus, although “the” may seem ordinary, it is a powerful building block of English.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an ablation applicator that uses a tubular body, an internal ablation-medium supply line with spaced openings, a temperature sensor, and a return line that defines the applicator’s active shape.
counterfactuals.output: An ablation applicator includes an elongate tubular body configured for insertion into or adjacent to target tissue. An ablation-medium supply line extends within the tubular body and includes a plurality of longitudinally spaced openings through which an ablation medium is delivered to an interior region of the tubular body. At least one temperature sensor is positioned to detect a temperature associated with the tubular body, the ablation medium, and/or surrounding tissue. A return line extends within the tubular body and is configured to receive the ablation medium after delivery through the spaced openings. The return line has a predetermined configuration and sufficient structural rigidity to define or maintain an active shape of the applicator. Circulation of the ablation medium through the supply line, the tubular body, and the return line provides controlled thermal ablation along an active region of the applicator, with operation adjustable in response to signals from the temperature sensor.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an intravascular thermal ablation device that can switch between a passive insertion mode and an active tissue-ablation mode.
counterfactuals.output:
An intravascular thermal ablation device can comprise a flexible catheter having a distal treatment assembly that selectively transitions between two operating states:

- **Passive insertion mode:** The distal assembly is collapsed into a low-profile, atraumatic configuration for advancement through a sheath and navigation within a vessel. Thermal elements are electrically disabled, and any expandable supports or electrodes are retracted or constrained against the catheter shaft.

- **Active tissue-ablation mode:** At the target location, the distal assembly is expanded—such as by deploying a basket, spiral, balloon, or articulated arms—to place one or more thermal applicators in controlled contact with the vessel wall. A generator then supplies radiofrequency, resistive, microwave, ultrasound, laser, or cryogenic energy to create a defined lesion in adjacent tissue.

A proximal handle or control system governs deployment and energy delivery, with an interlock preventing activation while the device is collapsed. Temperature, impedance, contact-force, and optionally blood-flow sensors provide feedback so a controller can regulate or terminate treatment. After ablation, the energy is disabled, the treatment assembly returns to its passive low-profile state, and the catheter is withdrawn.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key structural and functional features of a catheter-like applicator for thermally ablating blood-vessel tissue using a circulating ablation medium.
counterfactuals.output:
- **Elongated catheter body:** A slender, flexible shaft sized for intravascular insertion, with a proximal control/connection end and an atraumatic distal treatment end.

- **Closed circulation circuit:** Separate supply and return lumens carry a heated or cooled ablation medium to the distal region and back to an external temperature-control/pumping unit. The medium remains isolated from the bloodstream.

- **Heat-transfer treatment section:** The distal section has a thin, thermally conductive wall or expandable chamber through which heat is transferred from the circulating medium to the vessel wall. Other shaft portions may be thermally insulated to limit unintended injury.

- **Controlled flow distribution:** Internal channels, openings, baffles, or a coaxial-lumen arrangement direct the medium across the treatment section and promote uniform temperature along its circumference and length.

- **Vessel-wall contact or proximity:** The treatment section may expand, conform, or otherwise be centered against the vessel wall, improving circumferential heat transfer and potentially restricting local blood flow that could dissipate heat.

- **Thermal ablation function:** Circulation maintains the treatment region at a selected temperature for a selected time, causing controlled vessel-wall injury, collagen contraction, and eventual vessel closure. Treatment may be performed at a stationary segment or during catheter pullback.

- **Monitoring and safety features:** Temperature, pressure, and/or flow sensors can provide feedback, while a closed distal tip, pressure limits, and leak-resistant connections reduce the risk of medium escape, overheating, perforation, or treatment outside the target zone.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate technical patent language for an ablation device whose tubular applicator contains distributed fluid openings, an internal temperature sensor, and a shape-memory return line.
counterfactuals.output:
### Exemplary Patent Specification Language

#### Abstract

An ablation device includes an elongate tubular applicator configured for placement adjacent to or within target tissue. The tubular applicator defines a fluid delivery lumen and includes a plurality of fluid openings distributed along an treatment region of the applicator. A temperature sensor is disposed within the tubular applicator and is configured to generate a signal representative of temperature at the treatment region. A fluid return line extends through the tubular applicator and comprises a shape-memory material configured to bias at least a portion of the tubular applicator toward a predetermined configuration. During operation, fluid is supplied through the fluid delivery lumen and discharged through the distributed fluid openings to thermally interact with the target tissue, while return fluid is conveyed through the shape-memory return line. Sensor output may be used to regulate fluid temperature, pressure, flow rate, ablation duration, or delivered energy.

---

### Exemplary Independent Apparatus Claim

1. **An ablation device comprising:**

   an elongate tubular applicator having a proximal portion, a distal portion, and a treatment region disposed between the proximal portion and the distal portion;

   a fluid delivery lumen extending within the tubular applicator;

   a plurality of fluid openings formed through a wall of the tubular applicator and distributed along the treatment region, the plurality of fluid openings being in fluid communication with the fluid delivery lumen;

   at least one temperature sensor positioned within the tubular applicator and configured to provide a temperature signal indicative of a temperature associated with the treatment region; and

   a fluid return line extending within the tubular applicator and configured to convey fluid from the distal portion toward the proximal portion, at least a portion of the fluid return line comprising a shape-memory material configured to bias the treatment region toward a predetermined geometric configuration.

2. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the plurality of fluid openings are spaced longitudinally and circumferentially about the treatment region.

3. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the fluid openings have nonuniform dimensions selected to provide a predetermined distribution of fluid flow along the treatment region.

4. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the predetermined geometric configuration comprises a curved, arcuate, helical, annular, or substantially planar configuration.

5. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the shape-memory material comprises a nickel-titanium alloy.

6. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the fluid return line is transitionable from a delivery configuration to the predetermined geometric configuration in response to a temperature change, removal of a constraining member, or both.

7. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the at least one temperature sensor is disposed in a sealed sensor lumen and is thermally coupled to an exterior surface of the tubular applicator.

8. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the at least one temperature sensor comprises a thermocouple, thermistor, resistance temperature detector, semiconductor temperature sensor, or fiber-optic temperature sensor.

9. The ablation device of claim 1, further comprising a controller operatively coupled to the at least one temperature sensor, the controller being configured to control at least one of a fluid temperature, a fluid pressure, a fluid flow rate, an energy delivery parameter, or an ablation duration based at least in part on the temperature signal.

10. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the fluid return line is positioned eccentrically within the tubular applicator such that recovery of the shape-memory material imparts curvature to the treatment region.

11. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the fluid return line comprises a tubular shape-memory member defining a return lumen.

12. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the tubular applicator includes a porous, microporous, or perforated outer wall through which the fluid is delivered to tissue.

13. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the plurality of fluid openings are configured to discharge a heated fluid, a cooled fluid, a conductive fluid, or a phase-change fluid.

14. The ablation device of claim 1, further comprising at least one ablation electrode supported by the treatment region, wherein fluid discharged through the plurality of fluid openings modifies electrical or thermal coupling between the at least one ablation electrode and tissue.

15. The ablation device of claim 1, wherein the fluid return line is electrically isolated from an ablation-energy conductor extending through the tubular applicator.

---

### Exemplary System Claim

16. **An ablation system comprising:**

   a fluid source;

   a pump configured to deliver fluid from the fluid source;

   an ablation applicator comprising:
   
   - a tubular body defining a treatment region;
   - a delivery lumen coupled to the pump;
   - a plurality of fluid outlets distributed over the treatment region and in communication with the delivery lumen;
   - a temperature sensor located within the tubular body; and
   - a return conduit in fluid communication with the treatment region, the return conduit including a shape-memory structural portion configured to establish or maintain a selected shape of the treatment region; and

   a controller configured to receive a signal from the temperature sensor and regulate operation of the pump based on the signal.

17. The ablation system of claim 16, further comprising a thermal conditioning unit configured to heat or cool the fluid before the fluid enters the delivery lumen.

18. The ablation system of claim 16, wherein the controller is configured to reduce or interrupt fluid delivery when the signal indicates that a threshold temperature has been reached.

19. The ablation system of claim 16, wherein the controller is configured to maintain tissue-associated temperature within a predetermined therapeutic range by closed-loop adjustment of fluid flow.

20. The ablation system of claim 16, further comprising a negative-pressure source coupled to the return conduit.

---

### Exemplary Method Claim

21. **A method of ablating tissue, the method comprising:**

   positioning a treatment region of a tubular applicator relative to target tissue;

   causing a shape-memory return line disposed within the tubular applicator to bias the treatment region toward a predetermined configuration;

   supplying fluid through a delivery lumen of the tubular applicator;

   discharging the fluid through a plurality of fluid openings distributed along the treatment region;

   returning at least a portion of the fluid through the shape-memory return line;

   measuring a temperature associated with the treatment region using a temperature sensor disposed within the tubular applicator; and

   controlling an ablation parameter based at least in part on the measured temperature.

22. The method of claim 21, wherein causing the shape-memory return line to bias the treatment region comprises withdrawing the tubular applicator from a constraining sheath.

23. The method of claim 21, wherein controlling the ablation parameter comprises adjusting fluid temperature, fluid flow rate, fluid pressure, applied electrical power, or treatment duration.

24. The method of claim 21, further comprising circulating the fluid in a substantially closed fluid circuit between the delivery lumen and the shape-memory return line.

25. The method of claim 21, wherein discharging the fluid comprises distributing the fluid substantially uniformly along the target tissue despite a pressure gradient within the delivery lumen.

---

### Additional Detailed-Description Language

The tubular applicator may be formed from one or more flexible, biocompatible polymers and may include reinforcement layers, electrically insulating layers, radiopaque markers, or combinations thereof. The fluid openings may be arranged in rows, staggered arrays, helical patterns, circumferential bands, or location-specific patterns selected according to a desired ablation profile. Opening diameter, density, orientation, and spacing may vary along the treatment region to compensate for pressure loss and promote uniform fluid delivery.

The return line may perform both a fluid-conveyance function and a structural-shaping function. In certain embodiments, the return line is formed wholly or partly from a superelastic or thermally activated shape-memory alloy. The return line may be shape-set to a treatment configuration and elastically constrained in a relatively straight configuration during insertion. Upon release from a sheath or other constraint, the return line may recover toward the treatment configuration and thereby cause the tubular applicator to conform to an anatomical surface or surround at least part of a target structure.

The temperature sensor may be positioned proximally, centrally, or distally within the treatment region. Multiple temperature sensors may be distributed along the treatment region to permit spatial temperature monitoring. A thermally conductive member may extend between a sensor and the applicator wall while isolating the sensor from direct fluid flow. Sensor measurements may be corrected to account for fluid temperature, ambient temperature, thermal lag, or sensor position.

Fluid delivered through the openings may directly heat or cool tissue, irrigate an electrode-tissue interface, alter local electrical impedance, or transport thermal energy produced by another ablation modality. Suitable ablation modalities may include radiofrequency, microwave, resistive, ultrasound, laser, cryogenic, or fluid-mediated thermal ablation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
